title: Chicken Francese
subtitle: Egg-battered chicken cutlets in a lemon butter sauce
excerpt: Chicken Francese is an Italian-American classic where thin chicken cutlets are dipped in seasoned flour then egg before being pan-fried golden. A lemony pan sauce built on butter and chicken stock finishes the dish in minutes.
sourceNotes: Chicken Francese was developed by Italian immigrants in New York in the mid-twentieth century. It draws on the Italian uova al burro technique of egg-battering and has become a fixture of Italian-American red-sauce restaurant menus.

content.text: Pound the chicken breasts between two sheets of cling film to an even 5mm thickness. Even thickness means even cooking so no part dries out before the other is done.
Set up a dredging station with the seasoned flour in one shallow dish and the beaten eggs in another.
Dust each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in the beaten egg to coat.

Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Work in batches to avoid crowding. Remove to a warm plate.
Add the lemon slices to the pan and cook for 1 minute per side until slightly caramelised.
Pour in the stock and lemon juice. Scrape up any golden bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Swirl in the remaining butter, add the capers and parsley. Return the chicken to the pan for 1 minute to warm through. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Egg coating is falling off the chicken.
items.cause: The chicken was not dusted in flour before the egg dip.
items.fix: Always coat in flour first. The egg needs flour to grip.

items.cause: Butter was added to a very hot pan and split.
items.fix: Reduce heat before swirling in the final butter.
